inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + beta 1.2 x China/HK equity risk premium 6.5% = 9.6%, plus ~0.9pp for a May-2025 IPO with a thin H-share float and limited coverage = 10.5% standard. SANITY-CHECK FIX (Step 8c.5, rule 2, structural WACC premiums, applied 2026-10-18): the first build at 10.5% implied P/B 9.2x and EV/EBITDA 24.1x against the stock's single listing-year history (5.5x / 13.8x), and the diagnosis named cyclicality and a regulatory single point of failure. Explicit premiums added on top of 10.5%: concentrated geographic risk (>99% of stores in mainland China, earnings entirely exposed to one country's consumer) +1.0pp; regulatory single-point-of-failure (PRC franchise/food-safety licensing, preferential 15% EIT rates worth RMB17m/yr that can be withdrawn, CSRC filing control over future raises) +0.5pp; post-IPO illiquidity and overhang (pre-IPO lock-ups expiring 7 Nov 2026, 23% one-day drop in Aug 2026 on a lock-up notice) +0.5pp. Total 12.5%. Net-cash balance sheet, so WACC equals the cost of equity. The SAME 12.5% is used in all three scenarios: business risk (category saturation, closures, competition) is priced in the scenario flows and weights, country/regulatory/liquidity risk in the rate - each charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest, both read off the financing section: FY2025 46.5 + 3.1 = RMB49.6m, 1.1% of revenue; H1 FY2026 24.0 + 2.5 = 26.5m, 1.0%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (RMB127.9m at 30 June 2026) are excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 PP&E depreciation 21.5 + intangibles amortisation 2.7 = 24.2m, 0.54% of revenue). ebitda_margin_path is the post-IFRS-16, pre-SBC operating EBITDA margin ex interest and fair-value gains (FY2025 17.3%, 17.6% adding back RMB11.6m one-off listing expenses; H1 FY2026 17.6%).
inputs.nci_treatment: None - no non-controlling interests; profit attributable to owners equals group profit.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (routing table row 2: non-US operating company; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections a, b, d, f applied). Auntea Jenny is a franchise-led freshly-made tea chain (13,155 stores, 13,120 franchised, 35 self-operated) earning revenue from ingredient/packaging/equipment sales and service fees to franchisees - a capital-light operating company with a stream of free cash flow, not a bank/REIT/LIC. FIRST VALUATION (no memory entry, no prior DCF). HISTORY IS SHORT: three full fiscal years of P&L (FY2022-FY2025) and two of cash flow (FY2024-FY2025), listed 8 May 2025; FY2024 revenue fell 1.9% before FY2025 +36% and H1 FY2026 +42%, so the growth record is volatile and the base path deliberately fades hard. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 = FY2026, of which H1 is reported (+42.4% revenue, stores +39% YoY, closures 556 vs 645). Cash-tax path ramps from ~23% (H1 FY2026 cash tax 87.1/PBT 415.5 = 21%; FY2025 cash tax paid 178.9 = 26.5% of PBT) to the 25% PRC statutory rate as the 15% Western-Region/Hengqin subsidiary preferences (worth RMB16.9m in FY2025) are assumed to lapse. Working capital: franchisee prepayments (contract liabilities) and supplier payables fund inventory and receivables, so growth RELEASES cash (FY2025 ~13% of the revenue increase); wc_capture is set below that (8% base) and the engine shrinks the tailwind automatically as growth fades, and turns it into an outflow in the bear case's shrinking years. Terminal cap multiples (15x base, 18x bull, 12x bear) sit below the Gordon values at 10.5% WACC in every scenario, so Gordon binds; they are there to stop slider runaway. Price is an HKEX regular close, not after-hours.
inputs.street_vs_house_note: SBC is small (1.3% of FY2025 revenue, 0.9% in H1 FY2026) so the house/street band is narrow; band_position is reported but carries little information.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle revenue CAGR, first to last available year (FY2022 RMB2,199m to FY2025 RMB4,466m = 26.6%). Equity CAGR is not usable: book value was inflated by the RMB117m pre-IPO capital injection (2024) and the RMB288m IPO (2025). Sanity-check rule 3 (cap growth at the through-cycle CAGR) is met from year 2 onward in every scenario; year 1 (FY2026, base 34%) is left above the cap because H1 FY2026 is already reported at +42.4% with stores +39% YoY, and capping it would require H2 to grow ~12% against a network that is 25-30% larger than a year ago.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 74.1% diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (26.7%) and EPS (44.6%): the divergence is capital raised (pre-IPO injection RMB117.1m in FY2024, IPO net proceeds RMB264m in FY2025), not retained earnings compounding. EPS outgrew revenue because operating margin rose from 6.8% (FY2022) to 11.2% (FY2025) net; the FY2024 revenue dip (-1.9%) was a franchisee-destocking/consolidation year. Owner-FCF series exists only for FY2024 (276.9) and FY2025 (616.4): the +123% is mostly the FY2025 working-capital release and is not a trend.
historical_growth.notes: History is 3 P&L years and 2 cash-flow years. Reported-FCF growth FY2024->FY2025 was +82%; owner-FCF growth +123% because FY2024 lease cash (61.7) was larger than FY2025 (49.6) and SBC was flat - SBC is NOT growing faster than cash flow here (57.8 -> 57.4 -> H1 23.9).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +34%: H1 reported +42.4%; H2 laps a +63% H2 FY2025 comp but average store count is still ~25-30% higher YoY (11,458 at end-2025 -> 13,155 at June 2026), so H2 ~+28-30% gives ~RMB5.98bn. FY2027 +18%: opening pace (2,253 in H1 FY2026) cannot persist against a national tea-shop count that is already shrinking; store growth ~12-15% plus modest per-store purchasing growth and overseas (61 stores). From FY2028 the category is treated as mature: growth fades 12 -> 9 -> 7 -> 6 -> 5 -> 4 -> 3.5 -> 3, ending at ~RMB11.4bn in FY2035 (2.5x FY2025, roughly 20-22k stores at FY2025 revenue/store). Terminal 2.5% in RMB, below China nominal GDP.
base.margin_rationale: Operating EBITDA (pre-SBC, ex non-operating income) held near the FY2025/H1 FY2026 level of 17.6% with ~90bp of scale leverage over ten years; gross margin has been stable at 31.2-31.6% for five periods and management is spending on franchisee support, coffee rollout and cold-chain, so no large expansion is assumed.

scenario_narratives.base: Store network keeps growing but at a decelerating pace as the mass-market tea category consolidates: FY2026 lands around RMB6.0bn on the reported H1 run-rate, FY2027 adds ~18% as openings normalise to ~1,500-2,000 net a year against a ~10-12% closure rate, then growth fades to low-single digits by the early 2030s as the national shop count stops growing and the company's lower-tier-city whitespace fills. Operating EBITDA margin drifts from 17.6% to 18.5% on procurement scale, offset by continued franchisee-support, coffee and cold-chain spending; gross margin stays ~31.5%. Cash tax ramps to the 25% statutory rate as regional preferences lapse. Working capital keeps releasing cash while the system grows (franchisee prepayments and supplier terms), shrinking to nothing as growth normalises. Overseas (61 stores) is a free option, not modelled explicitly.
scenario_narratives.bull: Auntea Jenny consolidates the number-three/four slot behind Mixue and Guming: openings stay above 2,000 a year through FY2028 as weaker regional chains exit and their franchisees migrate, the H1 FY2026 improvement in closures persists, coffee machines and the 'Daily Health+' line lift per-store purchasing, and overseas (UK, Australia, Indonesia, US, Korea, Malaysia) scales to several hundred stores. Revenue compounds ~38% / 25% / 18% / 13% before fading; operating EBITDA margin reaches 20% on procurement and logistics leverage; working-capital release is a little larger (10% capture); terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The category's saturation reaches Auntea Jenny's core lower-tier-city turf: Mixue's scale pricing and Guming's density squeeze a second-tier brand, closures climb back above the FY2025 rate of ~12% while openings dry up, and the network peaks in FY2027 then shrinks ~5% over FY2029-FY2030 as a soft Chinese consumer cuts small-ticket discretionary spend. FY2026 still grows 28% because H1 is in the bank. Price support for franchisees and higher marketing cut operating EBITDA margin to 14.5%; the working-capital tailwind reverses into an outflow in the shrinking years; preferential tax rates lapse immediately (25% from year 1); terminal growth 1.5% and a 12x cap. The company stays profitable and net cash throughout - this is a value trap, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the industry evidence (national tea-shop count shrinking net, sector growth down to single digits), the company's own 12% FY2025 closure rate, its second-tier brand position in Mixue's price band, a 2.5-year financial record that already contains one revenue-decline year (FY2024), and the 7 Nov 2026 lock-up expiry overhang. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs three independent things - openings staying above 2,000/yr through saturation, closures continuing to fall, and overseas scaling - to go right together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Auntea Jenny as a capital-light franchise supply-chain business on owner free cash flow: EBITDA before share awards and ex non-operating income, less share awards, full lease cash, D&A ex right-of-use, cash tax ramping to 25%, light capex, and a working-capital release that is explicitly a function of growth rather than a flat margin. The RMB2.44bn of cash, deposits and wealth-management products (RMB23/share, ~HK$27 - nearly half the market price) is added once in the bridge with its income stripped from the flows, net of the two dividends paid since the June balance sheet. The single most important judgment is the growth fade: the 40%-plus run-rate is a store-opening wave in a category whose total shop count is already contracting, so the base case halves it within two years and reaches low single digits by year 7 rather than extrapolating. The price at the 52-week low implies the market is pricing something close to or below the bear path; the valuation says what you get if the business merely stops growing, and what the upside is if it does not.
key_risks_to_valuation: Store-opening pace collapses faster than the fade: if net openings turn negative in FY2027 rather than FY2029, year-2 to year-4 revenue is ~15-25% below base

Franchisee economics: a closure rate back above 12% with weaker openings would also reverse the working-capital tailwind (contract liabilities and payables unwind), which the base case assumes keeps releasing cash while the system grows
Margin: price competition with Mixue/Guming or franchisee subsidy programmes could push operating EBITDA margin below the 14.5% bear floor; gross margin has only five periods of history
Tax: the 15% preferential rates for Western-Region/Hengqin subsidiaries are assumed to lapse by year 3; if they are withdrawn retroactively or expanded, the cash tax path moves +/-2pp

Cash pile: RMB763m of the 'cash' is bank wealth-management products at fair value; a credit event in those products or trapped-cash/withholding frictions on repatriation to H-share holders would cut the bridge
Currency: RMB flows converted at 1.1724 HKD/CNY; a 5% RMB move shifts the HKD value ~5%, and refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate
Governance/overhang: concentrated pre-IPO holders, extended lock-ups expiring 7 Nov 2026, thin float - the August 2026 23% one-day drop shows how little liquidity there is

sanity_check.fix_applied: First build (WACC 10.5%, weighted IV HK$164.15) tripped on implied P/B 9.23x (>1.5x the 10yr max 5.55x) and EV/EBITDA 24.1x (>1.5x the 10yr max 13.8x); the history is a single listing year (FY2025) so the 'range' is one point. Fix per Step 8c.5 rule 2: explicit WACC premiums of +2.0pp (concentrated single-country China consumer exposure +1.0, PRC regulatory/preferential-tax single point of failure +0.5, post-IPO illiquidity and lock-up overhang +0.5) taking all three scenarios from 10.5% to 12.5%, documented in inputs.wacc_rationale. Rule 1 (mid-cycle FCF) was not applied: FY2025 is not a cyclical peak and the component build already fades the FY2025 working-capital release with growth. Rule 3: selected_growth_rate set to the through-cycle CAGR 26.6%; growth paths are below it from year 2 in every scenario, year 1 is anchored to the reported H1. Rule 4 (exit-multiple cap): the engine caps on FCF; the historical 13.8x SBC-adjusted EV/EBITDA converts to ~20x terminal owner FCF in the base case, so the existing 15x/18x/12x FCF caps are already tighter than the historical-range caps and Gordon binds in every scenario.
